title: Screw-clamp feed-through terminal block, 4 mm² class, grey

sources.citation: real-world (product class): screw-clamp feed-through DIN-rail terminal blocks of the 4 mm² class are 6.2 mm wide, about 47.7 mm long and 47.5 mm high on a 35 × 7.5 rail (a maker’s published datasheet, read 2026-11-12). Drawn 6 × 48 × 47 mm: the width rounded down to whole mm (so 10 blocks take 60 mm, not 62). Grey, the usual colour for line conductors.
game-design: two clamps, one at the top (1) and one at the bottom (2), 30 mm off the rail; conductors enter the top and bottom faces. Not taken from a product drawing.

game-design: clips onto a 35 mm top-hat rail (IEC 60715, cited by number), 6 mm along it, centred on the rail: its origin sits 45 − 24 = 21 mm above the mount origin (DIN 43880’s 90 mm modular-device line, ADR 0015 note 7), so its 48 mm body spans the rail centreline ± 24 mm.

real-world (product class): the 4 mm² screw feed-through class takes 26–10 AWG copper (of which 22–10 is used here; UL/CSA 30 A, 600 V), solid or stranded, stranded in a ferrule up to 4 mm², with a 9 mm strip and an M3 clamp screw tightened to 0.6–0.8 N·m (a maker’s datasheet, read 2026-11-12). The marked 0.6 N·m is the fictional block’s, at the low end of that range; NFPA 70-2023 Art. 110.14(D) (cited by number) requires the marked value. No UL 486A-B torque table is used.

game-design: the ±1 mm strip tolerance, the 8 mm cage depth (inside the 9 mm strip), the rising-cage (box) clamp type and the 1-rated / 2-fit rule. The real class allows two conductors of equal size only up to 1.5 mm² (about 16 AWG); the game lets two of any size fit and shares the clamp force (a documented abstraction, content caveats).

game-design: unverified. Terminal-block clamp screws commonly take a slotted blade, many with a Pozidriv combination head (common practice, not read from one datasheet); the drive type is a name and its size is not modelled.

game-design: each screw clamp takes the branch-circuit screw class’s contact resistance, 0.3 mΩ at the marked torque with copper at 20 °C (NBS Building Science Series 103, 1977, measured 0.2 to 0.5 mΩ on good branch-circuit screw terminals; ADR 0018 §4.1), and its calibrated 0.026 W/K heat path (§3.3). A terminal-block voltage-drop acceptance (at most 3.2 mV per block, two clamps, at a DC test current of 0.1 × the rated section’s current) gives at most 1.0 mΩ per block at 4 mm² (3.2 A); the model’s two clamps at 0.3 mΩ (0.6 mΩ, plus the ideal bridge) sit inside it. Read on a maker’s terminal-block test page (read 2026-11-12: https://www.phoenixcontact.com/en-ch/quality-tests-for-terminal-blocks/electrical-tests-terminal-blocks), which attributes the test to IEC 60947-7-1, IEC 61984 and UL 1059 (cited by number only; the standards themselves unverified). The cage’s heat capacity, 0.5 J/K, is a physics estimate: about 1.3 g of brass and steel × about 380 J/(kg·K).
